claims.claim: Think of a flight recorder. It keeps every move, so you can replay it. Screen: 'flight recorder   every move, kept'.
claims.source: https://www.ntsb.gov/news/Pages/cvr_fdr.aspx (read 2026-11-13, round 3): "The FDR onboard the aircraft records many different operating conditions of the flight." and "With the data retrieved from the FDR, the Safety Board can generate a computer animated video reconstruction of the flight."

FAIL' or '... ERROR' in either log. 925:780-782 and 853:784-786: 'Ran 624 tests ... FAILED (failures=1, skipped=25)'. Traceback 925:772-777: 'tests/test_vsl.py, line 357 ... AssertionError: 'BLOCK' != 'CLEAR' : the independent claim verifier still blocks: ['film shows init/ui/diff/--only and 7 agents; public main (baf5d02) has none of them and 3 agents', 'end card shows the site address ... which did not resolve at check time', "b19 'see every step and undo any of it' overstates ..."]'. tests/test_vsl.py:356-358 asserts only v.get("overall") == "CLEAR" for brand/vsl/claims-verified.json. GitHub API (read 2026-11-13) https://api.github.com/repos/Johnbjoseph-cybersec/rewindagents/actions/runs/43438869001/jobs: job 131930936925 'test (ubuntu-latest, python3)' head_sha 327d9b6fc698f09e01feca645042d133f8978bef conclusion failure, completed 14:02:29Z; job 131930937853 'test (macos-latest, python3)' same sha, conclusion failure, completed 14:03:21Z; in both, the failed step is 'Run python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v'.
claims.note: Settled. In both logs exactly one test fails. It fails at its last assertion (line 357), so the checks before it passed: claims.json has no BLOCK, blocked_in_scripts is 0, and beats_sha256 matches beats.json. That last match means the film text has not changed since the claim review. The failing assertion checks nothing except that the committed claims-verified.json says overall CLEAR. That file is the verifier's 2026-11-12 verdict against baf5d02, and its three blocks were resolved in round 3 (public main now has the features, the site resolves, b19 was reworded). The red run therefore reflects my own out-of-date verdict and does not show any film claim to be wrong. Every content test passed on both operating systems: test_vsl (12 other tests), test_site, test_demo, test_narration, test_launch, test_diff, test_rewind, test_rewind_only and test_ui. The logs are consistent with the API: same job IDs, sha and failing step, and end times that match the log timestamps. The failure message also quotes the committed file word for word. One correction to round 3: I said the run 'failed'. The API shows run status in_progress with conclusion null, because a third job (Windows) has not finished. See unverified.
